slot.brief: Four simple statements on NH3/PH3/AsH3 trends (boiling point, thermal stability, bond angle, basicity); pick the correct ones via codes.

stem: Consider the following trends for the Group 15 hydrides: (I) boiling point: NH₃ > AsH₃ > PH₃; (II) thermal stability: PH₃ > NH₃ > AsH₃; (III) bond angle: NH₃ > PH₃ > AsH₃; (IV) basicity: AsH₃ > PH₃ > NH₃. Which statements are correct?

verdicts.working: NH₃ has the highest boiling point due to hydrogen bonding, and AsH₃ boils above PH₃, so I is true. Thermal stability and basicity decrease down the group, making II and IV false. Bond angle decreases down the group, so III is true.

working:
Boiling points: NH₃ > AsH₃ > PH₃ (hydrogen bonding; then increasing molar mass).
Thermal stability: NH₃ > PH₃ > AsH₃.
Bond angles: NH₃ > PH₃ > AsH₃.
Basicity: NH₃ > PH₃ > AsH₃.
Correct statements: I and III.

Independent check: NH₃ has the highest boiling point due to hydrogen bonding, and AsH₃ boils above PH₃, so I is true. Thermal stability and basicity decrease down the group, making II and IV false. Bond angle decreases down the group, so III is true.
solution:
NH₃ has the highest boiling point due to hydrogen bonding; among PH₃ and AsH₃, boiling point increases with molar mass. Hence, (I) is true.
Thermal stability and basicity decrease down Group 15, so (II) and (IV) are false. Bond angle also decreases down the group: NH₃ > PH₃ > AsH₃, so (III) is true.
Thus, statements I and III are correct.
